zh.title: 从形成推断到今天：同一颗地球的证据旅程
zh.intro: 先看整球的定性变化，再接近一个合理的局部例子，最后检查材料留下的线索。三种观察层次共用当前年代与事件，不能互相替代证据。

viewQualifications.globe: 整球为定性教学重建；古海陆与冰雾不是实测复原。地月距离和小天体尺寸经过展示缩放。
viewQualifications.local: 与当前阶段相关的合理局部例子，不是从球面标记地点实测或精确复原的场景。
viewQualifications.evidence: 放大的教学模型，非样品照片或扫描；矿物、细胞、生物和层理不共用真实比例。真实证据需结合来源中的测量与地质背景。

zh.playbackQualification: 先停留观察，再加速跨时；进度不是地质速率。完整线性年代尺可展开查看。
zh.cueQualification: 核心、熔融、水、陆、冰、雾、植被与撞击提示均为独立的0—1绘图强度，不是实测百分比、浓度、概率或守恒预算。
zh.continuity: 切换观察层次保留同一年代、事件与选中的展示位置；回退只是重新取样，不把推断改成古代录像。

formation.label: 盘中的物质，怎样聚成地球？
formation.question: 一颗行星能从分散的小颗粒开始吗？
formation.seeing: 观察尘粒、小天体与长大的原始地球；接近表面，比较粗糙冷壳、暴露熔体和其中缓慢变化的热纹理。
formation.local: 近景放大同一颗原始地球表面的冷壳与熔体高低差；冷壳不等于现代板块，流纹也没有标定真实速度。
formation.evidence: 陨石中的矿物与放射性时钟、其他年轻恒星周围的盘，分别约束早期材料和行星形成模型。
formation.qualification: 形成过程是基于证据的推断；45.4亿年是沿用的近似地球年龄，不是吸积完成的精确时刻。尘粒、距离与播放速度不等比例。 热熔体与暂时冷却表皮展示形成过程中的一种片段，不代表早期地球每个时刻的统一外观或实测熔融比例。

separation.label: 受热以后，内部怎样重新分配？
separation.question: 金属与岩石会一直均匀混在一起吗？
separation.seeing: 在同一颗热的原始地球中观察金属富集区域与外部硅酸盐的分离。
separation.local: 局部剖面展示大小不一的金属团拉长、分散并向内富集，中央富集区随展示过程增强；这不是拍到的古地核或完整流体计算。
separation.evidence: 不同陨石保存金属与硅酸盐材料；它们帮助比较行星分异，并不是从地球地核取出的样品。
separation.qualification: 约45亿年的路标不表示分异在一天内完成，也不表示今天固态内核在那时形成；颜色与层厚不代表测量。

moon.label: 一次大碰撞，能解释月球的来历吗？
moon.question: 月岩给形成假说设置了哪些条件？
moon.seeing: 先观察撞击体接触原始地球，再看碎屑向外分布、轨道物质逐渐聚集；喷出物与月球不会在接触前提前出现。
moon.local: 近景只是大碰撞框架的一种教学构型；物体比例、轨道与时间都未作动力学求解。
moon.evidence: 月球样品的组成与高温历史、地月材料比较和轨道条件共同检验模型；放大的颗粒不是撞击诊断测量。
moon.qualification: 大碰撞是当前主要的月球形成假说；具体时间、初始条件和物质混合仍有研究空间。它与分异共用约45亿年路标，不是同一个事件。 碰撞体、盘与地月间距没有共用真实比例；动作时长不是实际形成时间。

water.label: 冷却后的世界，哪里留下水的线索？
water.question: 一粒晶体怎样记录已经消失的环境？
water.seeing: 观察冷却、表层岩石与水的教学转变；海陆块形状只帮助读图。
water.local: 近景代表岩石与液态水接触的一种可能环境，不是44亿年前某个海岸的复原。
water.evidence: Jack Hills古老锆石的年龄、化学和氧同位素支持源物质曾与液态水相互作用；生长分区被放大示意。
water.qualification: 这是间接的水相互作用证据，不是全球海洋地图、海水覆盖比例或生命检测；锆石彩带不是实测同位素读数。

life.label: 微小生命，怎样留下可保存的痕迹？
life.question: 最早保存下来的记录，等于生命的生日吗？
life.seeing: 从整球转到水边的微生物环境，寻找生命活动与岩石记录之间的联系。
life.local: 层状微生物席是合理的局部例子，不代表所有早期海岸或一个已知物种。
life.evidence: 约35亿年前的岩石中有微生物活动线索；研究结合沉积环境、结构与化学，检验非生物替代解释。
life.qualification: 记录表明生命到那时已经存在，不确定它何时起源；不能把每个早期叠层石都指定为产氧蓝细菌。细胞与层理为不同比例的教学模型。

oxygen.label: 有氧产生，为什么空气未必立刻变有氧？
oxygen.question: 来源与消耗怎样共同决定能否留存氧？
oxygen.seeing: 把产氧、消耗与长期留存联系起来；全球颜色变化只是提示，不是氧浓度曲线。
oxygen.local: 近景以含铁水体中的沉积过程展示一条可能途径；下方独立氧收支实验可比较相反结果。
oxygen.evidence: 岩石年代、硫同位素等记录约束大氧化；铁矿层帮助研究氧化还原，但部分铁氧化也可不依赖氧气。
oxygen.qualification: 约24—21亿年的背景包含波动；不是所有氧汇同时耗尽的全球开关，铁矿层也不是唯一的大气氧计。

cryogenian.label: 冰的线索，为什么会出现在古低纬度？
cryogenian.question: 全球推断需要把哪些地方的记录放在一起？
cryogenian.seeing: 观察广泛冰覆的一个示意状态，并把它与地质记录的问题相联系。
cryogenian.local: 近景展示冰与基岩、碎屑接触的合理例子；不声称是特定古大陆或纬度的复原。
cryogenian.evidence: 冰成沉积、搬运或擦痕线索与古地磁、年代共同支持低纬冰川推断；放大的碎屑组合不是一份真实样品扫描。
cryogenian.qualification: 约7.2—6.35亿年的成冰纪包含分开的冰期，不是持续85百万年的同一冰盖；完全海冰覆盖、开水区和生存环境需由证据与模型比较。

cambrian.label: 动物的身体与行为，怎样改变海底？
cambrian.question: 保存更容易，会怎样改变我们看到的化石记录？
cambrian.seeing: 整球提供寒武纪背景，近景观察海底动物、活动痕迹和沉积物之间的关系。
cambrian.local: 这是一组有依据的代表性海底形态，不是约5.39亿年前同一天、同一地点的群落复原。
cambrian.evidence: 化石形态与活动痕迹是观测线索；伯吉斯页岩等保存窗口记录的是寒武纪内的具体群落，不能等同于纪的开端。
cambrian.qualification: 动物并非在一天内一起出现，硬体与软体保存机会也不同；展示的双侧化石印痕为教学重建，不是标本扫描。

forests.label: 根系进入土壤，怎样改变环境？
forests.question: 地下保存的根，能告诉我们多少地上的森林？
forests.seeing: 观察植物、土壤与水的联系；植被提示强调局部生态变化，不代表全球森林覆盖率。
forests.local: 近景借助泥盆纪森林证据展示根与土壤的空间关系；不把这一站改画成后来的石炭纪煤沼。
forests.evidence: Cairo约3.86亿年前的古土壤和原位根网是直接记录；树冠与组织形态还需要其他化石和比较重建。
forests.qualification: 这里不宣称最古老森林，也不让森林必然变煤；埋藏、沉积与保存条件很重要。根与组织通道是放大的教学模型。

permian.label: 环境压力怎样成为生态危机？
permian.question: 更暖、含氧更少的海水，会给动物带来什么双重困难？
permian.seeing: 同一颗地球进入约2.52亿年前的危机背景；变化不等于全部生命瞬间消失。
permian.local: 近景比较受压力的海洋环境与仍存在的生命，作为生态后果的定性例子。
permian.evidence: 化石变化、岩石年代和环境指标与模拟互相检验；研究支持海洋变暖与缺氧对许多需氧动物造成压力。
permian.qualification: 这是多种压力相互作用的重建，不是单一烟雾开关或固定死亡比例；不同地区和生态功能的恢复不同步。化石为示意。

cretaceous.label: 一次撞击，为什么能影响远处的生命？
cretaceous.question: 阳光与食物网之间怎样传递影响？
cretaceous.seeing: 观察约6600万年前撞击及大气扰动的教学过程，继续追踪幸存生命。
cretaceous.local: 近景强调沉降材料与环境联系，不把局部撞击坑当作所有生态变化发生的地点。
cretaceous.evidence: 撞击坑、界线材料与化石变化相互约束；微观颗粒仅提示研究对象，不冒充诊断性冲击变形或元素测量。
cretaceous.qualification: 撞击有多种对应证据；同时期火山活动并不自动获得同等因果权重。消失的是非鸟类恐龙等许多群体，鸟类支系继续存活。

today.label: 今天，我们怎样读懂仍在变化的地球？
today.question: 眼前的过程，能帮助解释古老记录的哪些部分？
today.seeing: 观察岩石、水、冰与生命在同一世界中的联系，再回看前面的证据。
today.local: 近景代表现代土壤与水接触的一个例子；相似过程帮助比较，不意味着古今环境完全相同。
today.evidence: 现代岩石、生命活动与物质交换可以直接观察；这里的表面和微观对象仍是教学构造。
today.qualification: 程序生成的海陆仍是示意，不能当作卫星图或精确地图；地球历史不是通向人类的预设阶梯，也不是本模型对未来的预测。

ui.relatedIntro: 这里串起历史；下面的专题分别深入内部结构、生命、冰川和材料等机制。
ui.unavailable: 三维暂时不可用，已保留示意与证据。
ui.loading: 正在准备地球的历史场景……
ui.mapCredit: 可选现代地表底图：Solar System Scope / INOVE · CC BY 4.0
ui.transition: 这里是在两个代表观察段之间切换，并非当前年代的实测古地理影片。

zh.playbackDetails: 播放为相邻代表阶段分配相同展示时长：每段先保持该路标年代停留观察，再加速跨到下一阶段；进度不是地质速率。两条约45亿年路标保留不同身份，局部动作不按百万年标定。完整年代尺仍为线性。

en.title: From formation inferences to today: one Earth, several kinds of evidence
en.intro: Inspect a qualitative globe, approach a plausible local example, then examine clues in materials. All three lenses share the selected age and event; one lens cannot substitute for another kind of evidence.

viewQualifications.globe: A qualitative teaching reconstruction, not measured ancient geography or ice/haze coverage. Earth–Moon spacing and small-body sizes are rescaled for display.
viewQualifications.local: A plausible example related to this stage, rather than a measured or precisely reconstructed place selected on the globe.
viewQualifications.evidence: Enlarged teaching models, not sample photographs or scans. Minerals, cells, organisms and layers use different scales; actual evidence requires source measurements and geological context.

en.playbackQualification: Pause for observation, then an accelerated transition. The slider marks browsing position rather than a geological rate.
en.cueQualification: Core, melt, water, land, ice, haze, vegetation and impact cues are independent 0–1 drawing intensities, not measured percentages, concentrations, probabilities or conservation budgets.
en.continuity: Changing lens retains the same age, event and selected presentation position. Seeking backward resamples a model rather than turning inference into ancient footage.

formation.label: How did material in a disk build Earth?
formation.question: Can a planet begin with scattered small particles?
formation.seeing: Follow dust, small bodies and a growing proto-Earth; approach the surface to compare rough cooled skin, exposed melt and slowly changing hot material.
formation.local: The close view enlarges relief between cooled skin and melt on the same proto-Earth. These rafts are not modern tectonic plates, and flow textures have no calibrated speed.
formation.evidence: Meteorite minerals and radiometric clocks constrain early material history; observed disks around other young stars test planet-building models.
formation.qualification: Formation is an evidence-based inference. The retained 4.54 Ga estimate is not an exact accretion-completion date; particle sizes, distances and playback speed are not to scale. Exposed melt and temporarily cooled skin illustrate one part of the formation story, not a uniform appearance at every early time or a measured molten fraction.

separation.label: How did heating redistribute the interior?
separation.question: Must metal and rock remain evenly mixed?
separation.seeing: Within the same hot proto-Earth, compare an inward concentration of metal with surrounding silicates.
separation.local: The cutaway shows differently sized metal parcels elongating, dispersing and collecting inward as the central enriched region grows. It is neither footage of an ancient core nor a fluid-dynamics calculation.
separation.evidence: Meteorites preserve metal and silicate materials that help compare differentiation; they are not samples retrieved from Earth’s core.
separation.qualification: The approximate 4.5 Ga marker does not date a one-day process or the formation of today’s solid inner core. Colors and layer widths are illustrative.

moon.label: Can a giant collision explain the Moon?
moon.question: Which conditions must a model satisfy to match lunar rocks?
moon.seeing: Watch contact with proto-Earth before ejecta spreads and orbital material gathers; ejecta and the lunar aggregate do not appear before contact.
moon.local: The close view is one teaching configuration within the giant-impact framework, without solved trajectories, scale ratios or physical timing.
moon.evidence: Lunar composition and high-temperature history, Earth–Moon material comparisons and orbital constraints test models; enlarged grains supply no diagnostic impact measurements.
moon.qualification: A giant impact is the leading lunar-origin hypothesis; timing, initial conditions and mixing remain under study. It shares an approximate 4.5 Ga marker with differentiation while remaining a separate event. Impactor, disc and Earth–Moon spacing do not share a physical scale; display duration is not actual formation time.

water.label: Where did a cooling world leave clues to water?
water.question: How can a crystal preserve evidence of a vanished environment?
water.seeing: Follow an illustrative change from hot surfaces toward crust and water; land shapes only help read the scene.
water.local: The local view is a plausible example of rock–water contact, not a reconstructed 4.4 Ga coastline.
water.evidence: Ages, chemistry and oxygen isotopes in ancient Jack Hills zircons support liquid-water interaction in source material; growth zones are enlarged schematically.
water.qualification: This is indirect water-interaction evidence, not a global ocean map, measured water coverage or life detection. Colored zircon zones are not isotope readings.

life.label: How did tiny life leave lasting traces?
life.question: Is the earliest surviving record the birthday of life?
life.seeing: Move from the globe to a waterside microbial setting and connect activity with possible rock records.
life.local: The layered mat is a plausible local example, not every early shoreline or an identified ancient species.
life.evidence: Rocks around 3.5 Ga preserve microbial clues; researchers combine setting, structures and chemistry to test nonbiological alternatives.
life.qualification: Life was present by this record; its origin is not dated here. Not every early stromatolite identifies oxygen-producing cyanobacteria. Cells and layering use different enlarged teaching scales.

oxygen.label: Why need oxygen production not oxygenate the air immediately?
oxygen.question: How do sources and consumption together control retention?
oxygen.seeing: Connect production, consumption and long-term retention; globe colors are cues, not an oxygen-concentration curve.
oxygen.local: An iron-bearing water setting illustrates one deposition route. The separate oxygen ledger below permits genuinely different outcomes.
oxygen.evidence: Rock ages, sulfur isotopes and other records constrain oxygenation. Iron formations inform redox history, but some iron oxidation can occur without oxygen.
oxygen.qualification: The broad 2.4–2.1 Ga context includes fluctuations. There was no global switch when every sink ran out, and iron formations are not unique atmospheric oxygen gauges.

cryogenian.label: Why are glacial clues found at ancient low latitudes?
cryogenian.question: Which separate records must be combined for a global inference?
cryogenian.seeing: Inspect one illustrative state of widespread ice and relate it to questions asked of the geological record.
cryogenian.local: A local ice–bedrock–debris contact is plausible, without claiming a particular reconstructed ancient continent or latitude.
cryogenian.evidence: Glacial sediments, transport or abrasion clues, paleomagnetism and ages jointly support low-latitude glaciation. Enlarged debris is not a real sample scan.
cryogenian.qualification: The roughly 720–635 Ma Cryogenian contains separate glaciations, rather than one unbroken 85-million-year ice sheet. Complete sea ice, open water and habitats require record–model comparisons.

cambrian.label: How did animal bodies and behavior change the seabed?
cambrian.question: How might easier preservation change the fossil record we see?
cambrian.seeing: The globe supplies Cambrian context; a close view relates animals and activity traces to sediment.
cambrian.local: These evidence-informed representative forms do not reconstruct one community at one place exactly 539 Ma ago.
cambrian.evidence: Fossil shapes and activity traces are observations. Preservation windows such as the Burgess Shale sample particular communities within the Cambrian, rather than its beginning.
cambrian.qualification: Animals did not all appear on one day, and hard and soft parts preserve differently. The bilateral impression is a teaching reconstruction, not a specimen scan.

forests.label: How did roots entering soil change environments?
forests.question: How much of a forest above ground can roots below ground reveal?
forests.seeing: Connect vegetation, soil and water. The vegetation cue emphasizes local ecological change, not measured global forest cover.
forests.local: A Devonian example explores root–soil relationships without turning this stop into a later Carboniferous coal swamp.
forests.evidence: Cairo’s roughly 386 Ma paleosols and in-place root networks are direct records. Canopies and tissue forms require other fossils and comparative reconstruction.
forests.qualification: No oldest-forest claim is made, and a forest does not inevitably become coal: deposition, burial and preservation matter. Roots and tissue channels are enlarged teaching models.

permian.label: How can environmental pressure become an ecological crisis?
permian.question: What combined difficulties does warmer, less oxygenated water create for animals?
permian.seeing: The same planet enters the roughly 252 Ma crisis context without making all life disappear instantly.
permian.local: A stressed marine setting retains living forms as a qualitative example of ecological consequences.
permian.evidence: Fossil changes, rock ages, environmental indicators and models constrain one another; research supports warming and oxygen loss as stresses for many oxygen-dependent marine animals.
permian.qualification: This reconstruction combines pressures rather than a single haze switch or fixed death percentage. Regional and functional recovery differed; the fossil is illustrative.

cretaceous.label: How could an impact affect distant life?
cretaceous.question: How can reduced sunlight affect a food web?
cretaceous.seeing: Follow the roughly 66 Ma impact and an illustrative atmospheric disturbance, while retaining surviving life.
cretaceous.local: A close view connects deposited material and environmental change without placing every ecological consequence inside the crater.
cretaceous.evidence: Crater evidence, boundary materials and fossil changes constrain interpretation. Enlarged grains merely indicate research objects, without diagnostic shock deformation or elemental measurements.
cretaceous.qualification: Several corresponding records support impact; contemporary volcanism does not automatically receive equal causal weight. Many groups, including non-avian dinosaurs, vanished while bird lineages survived.

today.label: How can we read a world that is still changing?
today.question: Which parts of an ancient record can present processes help explain?
today.seeing: Connect rocks, water, ice and life in one world, then revisit the earlier evidence.
today.local: One modern soil–water contact illustrates comparison through similar processes, without making past and present environments identical.
today.evidence: Modern rocks, biological activity and material exchange can be observed directly; the displayed surface and microscopic objects are still teaching constructions.
today.qualification: Procedural land shapes are illustrative, not a satellite image or accurate map. Earth’s history is no prearranged ladder to humans, and this model does not predict its future.

en.playbackDetails: Playback gives adjacent representative intervals equal display time: each first holds its named age for observation, followed by accelerated change toward the next stage, rather than a geological rate. The two approximate 4.5 Ga markers retain separate identities; local motion is not calibrated in millions of years. The full geological ruler remains linear.
